# Kotlin Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: idiomatic Kotlin patterns that make Muse write Kotlin the way experienced Kotlin developers do. Covers seven areas: null safety through the type system (safe calls, the Elvis operator, non-nullable types by default, never force-unwrap with !!), immutability by default (val over var, copy() on data classes, immutable collections), sealed classes and interfaces for exhaustive when expressions over results and API errors, structured concurrency with coroutines and Flow (coroutineScope, supervisorScope, cancellation with ensureActive, Flow operators like debounce and mapLatest), extension functions that add behavior without inheritance, type-safe DSL builders with @DslMarker and lambda receivers, and Gradle Kotlin DSL build configuration. Every rule ships with GOOD/BAD code pairs, plus guidance on scope functions (when to reach for let, apply, also, run, with), property and interface delegation, sequences for lazy evaluation, and a catalog of anti-patterns (GlobalScope, deeply nested lets, mutable data classes, exceptions for control flow). Use when writing new Kotlin, reviewing pull requests, refactoring, designing modules or libraries, or configuring Gradle builds. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: patterns guide, you still write and own the code; dependency versions in the Gradle sample drift over time, check current releases; coroutines demand real understanding of...
